commands.name: trails-match
commands.help: link Ridge to Rivers' trails and the Greenbelt's closures to OpenStreetMap's paths, and build the routes and the valley-zoom network (the trails-match build; --dry-run)

commands.name: trails-export
commands.help: export OpenStreetMap's paved paths and pedestrian areas as base layers to $TVT_ARCHIVE/trails/export/ (marks the base bake out of date)

storage: Small. Ridge to Rivers: a layer description every 30 min (about 36 KB, nothing stored when unchanged); on an edit, or daily, the 271 trails are re-read (about 1 MB) and only changed trails add versions. A batch of new statuses for every trail adds 271 raw.record versions and 271 evt.event rows, each with its line: about 2-3 MB. Near zero in the dry season, a few MB a day at most in the wet one. Greenbelt: a few rows read hourly; kilobytes. The edit-date gate keeps one row per source in core's ops.layer_signature. OpenStreetMap (osm_paths): about 22k ways, a few dozen areas and about 150 routes, about 25 MB with indexes, versioned in place (no raw.record copies); grows only by changed OSM versions, at each hand-downloaded extract. Links and the build's tables (trails-match): a few MB, rewritten per build.
ethics: Both City layers are the City of Boise's, with a disclaimer and no license: used under the rule for state and local agency services (ch. 17 Q17), with a courtesy note to the City due. Until the City answers, rows stay internal; only aggregates (muddy or closed days per trail, closure counts) may be published, credited. That covers the links to OpenStreetMap's ways (trails.link, trails.matched_line, trails.way_agency), which carry the City's ids, and what the City's lines draw themselves (the 'trails.agency' tiles). The Trails layer's ways and valley-zoom network (trails.path, trails.path_lo: the 'trails.paths' tiles) carry nothing from the City: its states reach the map as feature-state only. The views that read the City's rows (agency_line, agency_state, way_agency) run with the reader's privileges, and the tile login is refused them. Staff names (R2R's Editor, and editor tracking's Creator, Editor, created_user and last_edited_user in either layer) are dropped at ingest. R2R's Condition is advice, not a closure order, and is labelled as R2R's. Query only: never an edit operation, never the Survey123 layer in R2R's web map. services1.arcgis.com's robots.txt answers 403 (no rules). OpenStreetMap is ODbL: credit "© OpenStreetMap contributors", and anything published from it stays ODbL; Geofabrik's robots.txt disallows scripted downloads, so extracts are downloaded by hand. Ways tagged private or no access are never drawn as trails (plan C18), unless foot, bicycle or horse is opened on them, and informal trails are drawn only close in, labelled, and hidden near closures.
